items.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position of the image formed by the mirror.
items.answer:
Given: focal length (f) = +15 cm, object distance (u) = −10 cm.
From the mirror formula, 1/f = 1/v + 1/u
1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/15 − 1/(−10) = 1/15 + 1/10 = (2 + 3)/30 = 5/30 = 1/6
v = +6 cm
The image is formed 6 cm behind the mirror (virtual and erect).
items.ocr: MinerU printed the last step as 'v = (2+3)/30 = 6 cm', collapsing the reciprocal; restored 1/v = 5/30 = 1/6 so v = +6 cm. LaTeX array of givens rewritten to plain text.

items.stem: What are the properties of the image formed by a plane mirror?
items.answer:
(i) The image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual and erect.
(ii) The size of the image is equal to that of the object.
(iii) The image formed is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.
(iv) The image is laterally inverted.

items.stem: Distinguish between convex mirror and concave mirror.
items.answer:
Convex mirror:
(i) The reflecting surface is curved outward.
(ii) The image formed is diminished and erect.

Concave mirror:
(i) The reflecting surface is curved inward.
(ii) The image formed may be real or virtual and either diminished or enlarged.
items.ocr: The printed answer is a two-column comparison; MinerU flattened it into one run of text. Re-split under the 'Convex mirror' and 'Concave mirror' headings it prints.

items.stem: Name the type of mirror used in a solar furnace. How is high temperature achieved by this device?
items.answer: A concave mirror is used in a solar furnace. The solar furnace is placed at the focus of the large concave reflector. The concave reflector focuses the Sun's heat rays on the furnace and so a high temperature is achieved.

items.stem: Identify the nature of the mirror and mention two characteristics of the image formed when magnification (m) = +6.
items.answer:
The mirror is concave (a positive magnification greater than 1 is produced by a concave mirror with the object between the pole and the focus).
(i) The image is virtual and erect.
(ii) It is 6 times enlarged than the object.

items.stem:
(a) What should be the position of the object, when a concave mirror is to be used (i) as a shaving mirror, and (ii) in torches producing parallel beam of light?
(b) A man standing in front of a mirror, finds his image having a very small head and legs of normal size. What types of mirrors are used in designing such a mirror?
items.answer:
(a) (i) The object should be between the pole and the focus of the concave mirror.
(ii) The object (the bulb) should be at the focus.
(b) (i) Small head — convex mirror.
(ii) Legs of normal size — plane mirror.

items.stem: Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm so as to obtain a two times magnified real image?
items.answer:
Since the image is real, m = −2 and f = −20 cm.
m = −v/u ⇒ −2 = −v/u ⇒ v = 2u
1/f = 1/u + 1/v
1/(−20) = 1/u + 1/(2u) = 3/(2u)
2u = −60 ⇒ u = −30 cm
The object should be placed 30 cm in front of the mirror (between C and F).
items.ocr: OCR produced 'f = -20 cos' and '-30 cos' for 'cm'; corrected. The garbled $$ array was rewritten step by step to reach the printed result u = −30 cm.

items.stem: Complete the diagram in your answer book and write the nature of the image formed.
items.answer: On completing the ray diagram, the refracted rays meet on the other side of the convex lens, so the nature of the image formed is real and inverted.

items.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show the position and nature of the image formed by a convex lens when the object is placed: (i) beyond 2F, (ii) between F and 2F.
items.answer:
(i) When the object is placed beyond 2F, the image is formed between F and 2F on the other side of the lens; it is real, inverted and diminished.
(ii) When the object is placed between F and 2F, the image is formed beyond 2F on the other side of the lens; it is real, inverted and enlarged.

items.stem: Name the type of lens that can be used as magnifying glass. Give reason(s) and draw a ray diagram to support your answer.
items.answer: A convex lens is used as a magnifying glass. When an object is placed close to a convex lens (between the optical centre and the focus), its erect, virtual and magnified image is formed, which is why it acts as a magnifying glass.

items.stem: To get a real and inverted image of same size as that of the object by a thin convex lens of focal length 20 cm, where should the object be placed? Draw a ray diagram to show image formation in this case.
items.answer: The object should be placed at 2F, i.e. at 40 cm from the optical centre of the lens. The image is then also formed at 2F on the other side and is real, inverted and of the same size as the object.

items.stem: An object is 2 m away from a lens, which forms an erect image one-fourth the size of the object. Determine the focal length of the lens. What type of lens is this?
items.answer:
Given: u = −2 m, m = +1/4 (image erect and diminished).
m = v/u ⇒ 1/4 = v/(−2) ⇒ v = −0.5 m
1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/(−0.5) − 1/(−2) = −2 + 0.5 = −1.5 = −3/2
f = −2/3 m ≈ −0.67 m
Since the focal length is negative, the lens is a concave (diverging) lens.
items.ocr: The worked solution came through almost entirely as OCR noise ('a = -2 m', fraction fragments, '-20.5'); reconstructed the standard steps so they reach the two printed results, f = −2/3 m and 'Lens is concave.'

items.stem: Two lenses of power −2.5 D and +1.5 D are placed in contact. Find the total power of the combination of lenses. Calculate the focal length of this combination.
items.answer:
Given: P₁ = −2.5 D, P₂ = +1.5 D.
Total power of the combination,
P = P₁ + P₂ = −2.5 D + 1.5 D = −1.0 D
Since P = 1/f (f in metre),
f = 1/P = 1/(−1) = −1 m = −100 cm
The focal length of the combination is −1 m.

items.stem: An object placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Write four characteristics of the image formed by the mirror.
items.answer:
Four properties of the image formed by the given convex mirror are:
(i) The image is always erect.
(ii) It is small in size (diminished).
(iii) It is virtual.
(iv) It is always formed behind the mirror, between the focus and the pole.

items.stem:
(i) Name the spherical mirror used as (a) Shaving mirror, (b) Rear view mirror in vehicles, (c) Reflector in search light.
(ii) Write any three differences between a real and a virtual image.
items.answer:
(i) (a) Shaving mirror — concave mirror. (b) Rear view mirror in vehicles — convex mirror. (c) Reflector in search lights — concave mirror.
(ii) (a) A real image can be obtained on a screen but a virtual image cannot be obtained on a screen.
(b) For a real image the reflected/refracted rays actually meet, while for a virtual image they only appear to meet.
(c) A real image is always inverted while a virtual image is always erect.

items.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 12 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm. List four characteristics of the image formed by the mirror.
items.answer:
Here f = R/2 = 15 cm, so the object at 12 cm lies between the pole and the focus. Therefore:
(i) The image is always erect.
(ii) It is big in size (enlarged).
(iii) It is virtual.
(iv) It is always formed behind the mirror.

items.stem: State the two laws of reflection of light.
items.answer:
(i) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
(ii) The incident ray, the normal to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence and the reflected ray from that point, all lie in the same plane.

items.stem: Differentiate a real image from a virtual image giving two points of difference.
items.answer:
Real ImageImage
1.Formed when reflected rays meet.Formed at point from which the reflected rays appear diverse.
2.Image is always inverted.always erect.
Read as: (1) A real image is formed where the reflected rays actually meet, whereas a virtual image is formed at the point from which the reflected rays appear to diverge. (2) A real image is always inverted, whereas a virtual image is always erect.

items.stem: An object of height 1.2 cm is placed before a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm so that a real image is formed at a distance of 60 cm from it. Find the position of an object. What will be the height of the image formed?
items.answer:
Given: hₒ = 1.2 cm, f = −20 cm, v = −60 cm.
1/u = 1/f − 1/v = 1/(−20) − 1/(−60) = 1/60 − 1/20 = (1 − 3)/60 = −2/60
u = −30 cm, so the object is 30 cm in front of the mirror.
hᵢ/hₒ = −v/u
hᵢ = −(−60)/(−30) × 1.2 = −2 × 1.2 = −2.4 cm
The image is 2.4 cm high and inverted (real).
items.ocr: The printed stem gives the object height as '1.2 m' while its own worked solution uses hₒ = 1.2 cm and returns hᵢ = −2.4 cm; the solution wins, so the stem records 1.2 cm.

items.stem: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm is placed at a distance of 12 cm from a wall. Calculate the distance from the lens where an object can be placed so as to form its distinct real image on the wall.
items.answer:
Given: v = +12 cm, f = +10 cm.
1/v − 1/u = 1/f
1/12 − 1/u = 1/10
1/u = 1/12 − 1/10 = (5 − 6)/60 = −1/60
u = −60 cm
The object should be placed 60 cm from the lens, on the side opposite the wall.
items.ocr: The stem prints 'focal lengths 10 cm'; read as 'focal length 10 cm'. The given block was split across a page boundary ('v = + 12 cm , f = + 10 c m'); rejoined.

items.stem: A concave mirror is known as a converging mirror while a convex mirror is known as diverging mirror. Explain why?
items.answer: A concave mirror converges a parallel beam of light falling on it to a point (its focus), so it is known as a converging mirror. On the other hand, a convex mirror diverges a parallel beam falling on it (the reflected rays appear to come from its focus behind the mirror), so it is known as a diverging mirror.
